title: Railway-signal cutlines and blocker mitigation playbook for API/Console/Runtime release
creator: Priya Nair
description: This ticket captures the operational playbook for hard cut decisions, scope-lock signaling, and rapid mitigation of blockers for the combined API / Console / Runtime release train. The playbook uses a railway-signal metaphor to make go/no-go decisions deterministic across engineering, product, design, docs, and GTM. It includes milestone gating rules, clear cut criteria, an escalation path, and a templated communications bundle for release notes and downstream customers.
milestones: Kickoff & alignment: 2025-11-10 - cross-functional alignment meeting to define primary SLOs and non-negotiables
Scope lock window opens: 2026-01-15 - feature freeze intent declared; all new surface-area changes require explicit approval
Feature complete checkpoint: 2026-02-28 - all planned features merged into release branch, blockers triaged
Code freeze: 2026-03-10 - no non-critical changes; exceptions via release lead approval
Docs & release-notes freeze: 2026-03-20 - final release notes and GTM assets locked for translation and legal review
Canary rollout window: 2026-04-05 - progressive rollout to internal customers and early partners
GA launch: 2026-04-30 - public announcement and customer migration guides published
cut_criteria: SLO alignment: latency and error-rate SLOs must be within 2x of baseline in performance tests
Regression threshold: critical regression rate <= 1% vs baseline on canonical workloads
Security sign-off: open security findings with severity >= High must be triaged and ownership assigned; unresolved High severity is a hard blocker
Blocking bugs: any P0 functional regression in core API or runtime behaviour is a hard stop
Feature toggleability: any non-trivial new surface must be behind a toggle and be rollbackable within 15 minutes
Data migration/compatibility: any migration with potential backwards-incompatibility must have automated rollback and test coverage
rollout_checklist: Confirm Dedicated capacity quotas for initial canary cohort
Allocate on-call rotation for release week across runtime, API, and console teams
Create fallback model routing rules for degraded runtime capacity
Validate observability dashboards and add token-level cost charts for new routes
Prepare incident runbook and postmortem template specific to this release
Authorities: release manager, runtime lead, security owner, PM, and design lead identified
release_notes_tasks: Consolidate feature bullets from ENG owners by 2026-03-01
Design to provide 2 screenshots per Console change by 2026-03-05
Security to provide a short summary of any cryptography/KMS changes
Performance team to provide before/after cost and p95 latency numbers
API changelog: list all breaking changes and explicit migration steps
Legal & compliance review: embargoed wording and partner attribution cleared by 2026-03-18
dependencies_details: ENG-22011 (batching improvements) must land by Feature complete or be scoped out
DES-1142 (Console UX modal for rollout controls) required for toggleability acceptance
PM-6147 (release-train-playbook) provides canonical signoff matrix to attach to this ticket
risk_mitigation: Risk: unexpected performance regression in long-tail token sequences. Mitigation: run extended 48-hour load job and prepare quantized fallback model families
Risk: rollback inability due to schema changes. Mitigation: ensure compatibility flags and create an automated migration snapshot
Risk: docs lagging behind features. Mitigation: gating rule that docs freeze must pass peer review before Code freeze is lifted
Risk: partner communication delays. Mitigation: draft customer notices early and route through PM partner liaisons
decisions: Decision 2025-11-12: use a three-tier cut signal: green (go), amber (conditional), red (stop). Amber requires mitigation plan and explicit release lead sign-off.
Decision 2026-01-22: tolerate up to 1.5x p95 latency increase for non-tenant-critical routes during canary if overall error rates remain stable.
Decision 2026-02-02: public-facing breaking changes will be behind an opt-in beta for 30 days before GA
